predecessors.note: The same state under an earlier official English name (see notes): the republic was declared on 14 July 1958 and 'Republic of Iraq' has been the name since January 1992. Cliopatria's Iraqi Republic row ends in 2005; the iraqi-republic dossier (me-10-k) ends in October 2005 and names this one as successor.

correction.text: Iraq within its present frontiers, 438,317 km2 (infobox; the geography section gives 437,072 km2)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a gap: Cliopatria's Iraqi Republic row ends in 2005 and this row begins in 2014, leaving 2006-2013 with no shape. The outline of both neighbours is the same (1,686 and 1,685 cells in the gazetteer), so the 2014 outline is used. The constitution of 15 October 2005 (infobox) reaffirms the name 'Republic of Iraq'. The page names no territorial change between 2005 and 2013; its only border item is a December 2009 incident in which Iraq accused Iran of seizing an oil well on the frontier.

438,702 km2 for 2014-2023 against the infobox 438,317 km2 (ratio 1.001; the geography section's 437,072 gives 1.004). The shape is the whole country, as it should be for the state's claim: the land ISIL held from 2014 to 2017 and Kirkuk held by Kurdish forces are carried by the ledger (loss and gain against islamic-state and kurdistan-region), not by cutting the shape. The Kurdistan Region's autonomy ('autonomy was given to Kurds' after the 1991 uprisings, no date on the page) is not drawn. The 'Iran' in the seed's modern_countries is raster noise on the frontier.

Identical to 2014-2023; the Iraq page reports no border treaty or territorial change in 2024. Extended to 2026 by fx-32 (F184): Cliopatria's last row for the state is 2024, but the state continues; the Iraq page (opened 2026-11-01) describes Iraq as a 'democratic federal parliamentary republic' with dated items to 2025 and records no border treaty, demarcation or territorial change after 2023, so the 2024 outline holds to 2026 (no dissolve event; the compiler keeps a dossier without one alive through 2026). The Kurdistan Region stays the child (hierarchy.csv, constituent, supplies the tint).

ledger.note: 2005: the Republic of Iraq is reaffirmed by a new constitution. Infobox 'Current constitution: 15 October 2005'; the text has it approved by referendum in October 2005 with a 78% overall majority, followed by fresh parliamentary elections on 15 December 2005; the name 'Republic of Iraq' has been used 'since January 1992, reaffirmed in the 2005 Constitution' and the republic itself was declared on 14 July 1958. This is the same state as the Iraqi Republic row under a later official name; the date is chosen because Cliopatria's Iraqi Republic row ends in 2005. The page does not mention the transfer of sovereignty of 28 June 2004.

region.text: the governorates the page names: Al Anbar (Fallujah, Ramadi, Al Qaim), Nineveh (Mosul, Tal Afar, Sinjar), Kirkuk, Diyala and Tikrit

ledger.note: 2013: the war with ISIL begins. Infobox dates the war 30 December 2013 to 9 December 2017; the Iraq page has Sunni militants attacking in the 'Anbar campaign' of 2013. The zone is the governorates the page names (my reading of where the fighting was); it is paired with the end on 9 December 2017.

region.text: Al Anbar: Fallujah, Al Qaim and half of Ramadi

ledger.note: 2014: ISIL takes the cities of Anbar. ISIL and Baathist allies seized 'at least 70%' of Al Anbar Governorate by June 2014, including Fallujah, Al Qaim and half of Ramadi; a footnote has a revolt in Ramadi on the eve of the New Year 2014 after which ISIS gained control of Ramadi and Fallujah. Recorded for the whole governorate because the page gives a share, not a boundary.

2014: Kirkuk passes out of Baghdad's hands. Page silent on how and when: the page mentions only that ISIL captured parts of Kirkuk, and later says the Iraqi Army launched an offensive on 15 October 2017 'to recapture Kirkuk from the Kurdistan Region', which implies Kurdish control before it. The date June 2014 is a bridging judgment, not the page's.

region.text: Mosul, Tal Afar and most of Nineveh Governorate, and Tikrit

ledger.note: 2014: Mosul falls to ISIL. Between 4 and 9 June 2014 Mosul was attacked and later fell (10 June is when Maliki called for a state of emergency); ISIL also captured Tal Afar and most of Nineveh Governorate, parts of Kirkuk and Diyala, and Tikrit, all in the June offensive; the caliphate was announced on 29 June 2014 and at its height ISIL held 56,000 km2 of Iraqi territory with 4.5 million people. The page gives no date for Tikrit or Tal Afar and has Sinjar taken in August 2014 after the Peshmerga abandoned it.

region.text: parts of Kirkuk and Diyala governorates

ledger.note: 2014: ISIL holds pockets of Kirkuk and Diyala. The page says only that ISIL took 'parts of Kirkuk and Diyala' in the June offensive and does not say it captured Hawija; Hawija is placed here from its recapture in October 2017 (below), a bridging judgment.
2015: Tikrit is retaken. The Second Battle of Tikrit began on 2 March 2015 and lasted more than a month; the page gives no April date.
2015: Ramadi is liberated. ISIL captured the provincial capital in late May 2015; the Iraqi Army's recapture campaign began on 22 December 2015 and Iraq declared Ramadi liberated on 28 December.
2016: Fallujah is retaken. The Third Battle of Fallujah ended in June 2016 (the page gives no day).
2017: Mosul is captured. Iraqi Army forces captured Mosul on 10 July 2017.

region.text: Tal Afar and the rest of Nineveh Governorate except Sinjar

ledger.note: 2017: Tal Afar falls. The offensive was launched on 20 August and completed by 31 August 2017. The rest of the governorate is my reading; Sinjar is left to the October entry.
2017: Hawija is retaken. The offensive started in late September and was complete by 5 October 2017 (no exact day on the page).

2017: Iraq retakes Kirkuk from the Kurds. The Iraqi Army launched an offensive on 15 October 2017 to recapture Kirkuk from the Kurdistan Region, with help from the Talabani family and some PUK members; Masoud Barzani announced he would step down effective 1 November. The page does not mention the independence referendum of 25 September 2017.

2017: Sinjar is captured by Iraqi forces. 'Following the defeat of the Peshmerga and the capture of Kirkuk and Sinjar by the Iraqi armed forces' (the page's words; reviewer me-10-m corrected the quotation); the page names the Peshmerga as the side defeated but gives no separate date for Sinjar; the ledger has Sinjar lost to ISIL with Nineveh in June 2014 and the Kurdish recapture in between is not on the pages opened, so the counterpart is the Kurdistan Region as the page implies.

region.text: Al Anbar, the last strongholds Al-Qaim and Rawa

ledger.note: 2017: ISIL's last towns fall. Iraq captured Al-Qaim and Rawa, ISIL's last two strongholds, on 17 November 2017. The page names Al-Qa'im and Rawah, not the governorate; the region is the rest of Al Anbar as a reading, so confidence 2 (reviewer me-10-m).

region.text: the governorates the page names: Al Anbar (Fallujah, Ramadi, Al Qaim), Nineveh (Mosul, Tal Afar, Sinjar), Kirkuk, Diyala and Tikrit

ledger.note: 2017: the war against ISIL is declared won. Prime Minister Haider al-Abadi announced the end of the war on 9 December 2017 (a victory parade followed on 10 December); the Iraq page: 'In December 2017, when ISIS had lost all its territory in Iraq, the government declared victory.' ISIL kept up a lower-scale insurgency.

wars.outcome: Iraqi and allied victory (infobox, 30 December 2013 to 9 December 2017). ISIL took Fallujah and Ramadi, Mosul, Tikrit and Tal Afar in 2014 and at its height held 56,000 km2 of Iraqi territory; Iraq retook Tikrit (2015), Ramadi (December 2015), Fallujah (June 2016), Mosul (10 July 2017), Tal Afar (August 2017), Hawija (October 2017) and Al-Qaim and Rawa (17 November 2017).
wars.note: The page does not give Peshmerga operations (Kirkuk in June 2014) or the 2017 independence referendum.

wars.name: Iraqi-Kurdish confrontation of October 2017
wars.outcome: The Iraqi Army's offensive of 15 October 2017 captured Kirkuk and Sinjar from the Kurdistan Region; Barzani announced he would step down effective 1 November.
wars.note: The page is silent on the referendum that preceded it.

certainty.note: Treaty and survey frontiers of a modern state (the page says Iraq and Kuwait were working on a definitive demarcation agreement, with no date, and records a December 2009 incident in which Iraq accused Iran of seizing an oil well on the border). Exceptions: from 2014 to 2017 the lines of ISIL-held and Kurdish-held land (Mosul, Anbar, Kirkuk) are front lines, drawn by loss and gain events; the Kurdistan Region's internal boundary is not drawn.

notes: Pages used: 2 (the budget is 1-2). ONE STATE, TWO ROWS: the Iraq page has the republic declared on 14 July 1958 and the name 'Republic of Iraq' used since January 1992 and reaffirmed in 2005, so Cliopatria's 'Iraqi Republic' (1960..2005) and 'Republic of Iraq' (2014..2024), both Q796 and Wikipedia 'Iraq', are one state under successive official English names. The brief asked for one dossier under the earlier slug, but that slug is owned by batch me-10-k; their iraqi-republic.json (read on 2026-10-25) ends in October 2005 with a dissolve event and names republic-of-iraq as its successor, so the two files are joined at October 2005 and this dossier is the later phase of the same state (the colour agent should give both one colour). This file starts with the constitution of October 2005, adds a 2005-2013 keyframe for the years Cliopatria skips, and carries the 2013-2017 war. Not settled: (1) the 2003 invasion, the Coalition Provisional Authority and the occupation belong to iraqi-republic; the Iraq page does not mention an interim government or the 28 June 2004 transfer of sovereignty; (2) Kirkuk: the 2014 loss to the Kurdistan Region and the Hawija pocket are confidence 1 (page silent); (3) the Kurdistan Region has no dossier ('kurdistan-region', the slug me-10-k also uses; autonomy after the 1991 uprisings, no date on the page) and neither has the Islamic State ('islamic-state', 2014-2017 as a holder of land, type rebel; Cliopatria's Mujahideen row has a 68,889 km2 2014-2024 shape across Syria, Iraq and Turkey that is probably its Cliopatria stand-in); (4) Sinjar's recapture by Kurdish forces in between is not on the pages; (5) ISIL territory in Diyala and Salah ad-Din beyond Tikrit is not named by the page, so only the pockets above are recorded. Names the gazetteer lacks and the dossier uses: Hawija (Iraq, Kirkuk governorate, about 35.3 N 43.8 E) and Sinjar (Iraq, Nineveh, about 36.3 N 41.9 E).
